title: Sub-GHz Telemetry Radio
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a sub-GHz telemetry node operating in the 902–928 MHz ISM band.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Design a sub-GHz telemetry node for the 902–928 MHz ISM band

fixed_requirements.requirement: The radio must be a modern packet radio transceiver (device class fixed; specific part not).
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: ISM band using a modern packet radio transceiver and an MCU.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board must carry an MCU alongside the transceiver.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: using a modern packet radio transceiver and an MCU. Target materially longer range

fixed_requirements.requirement: The design must target materially longer range than a bare low-power radio would achieve.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Target materially longer range than a bare low-power radio

fixed_requirements.requirement: The brief names an appropriate front-end or PA/LNA solution as the means it contemplates for reaching that range, with inclusion conditional on being justified; it neither mandates a front end nor rules out other ways of gaining range.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: by including an appropriate front-end or PA/LNA solution if justified.
Provide USB-C, a battery input, and an SMA antenna connector.
Provide USB-C, a battery input, and an SMA antenna connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Provide an SMA antenna connector as the antenna interface (SMA, not a reverse-polarity or other family).
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Provide USB-C, a battery input, and an SMA antenna connector.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The RF layout must follow vendor RF reference layouts.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Follow vendor RF reference layouts and document the matching/filter network

fixed_requirements.requirement: The matching/filter network must be documented as a deliverable, not merely drawn.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: document the matching/filter network and power-current assumptions.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The power-current assumptions must be documented as a deliverable.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Follow vendor RF reference layouts and document the matching/filter network and power-current assumptions.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Where the brief is open, the design agent must make and document reasonable engineering decisions instead of inventing hidden user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic must not accumulate in the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Requirements the brief does state are authoritative: they may not be loosened, reopened as choices, or traded away in the course of making the open decisions.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open

open_decisions.decision: Which packet radio transceiver to use — vendor, part, modulation scheme (FSK/LoRa-class/other), interface, and package.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief specifies only "a modern packet radio transceiver" and names no device, vendor, or modulation family.

open_decisions.decision: Which MCU to use — architecture, memory, peripheral set, package, and whether radio and MCU are separate devices or a combined SoC/module.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says only "an MCU" and does not constrain family, performance, or integration level.

open_decisions.decision: Whether to fit a front end at all, and if so which topology: an integrated front-end module versus discrete PA, LNA and antenna switch.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief makes the front-end/PA/LNA conditional — "if justified" — so both inclusion and topology are the agent's call to argue.

open_decisions.decision: How "materially longer range" is quantified: target TX power, receive sensitivity, link budget, assumed antenna gain and path model, and what evidence closes the claim.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief gives a comparative goal with no distance, dBm, or dB figure attached.

open_decisions.decision: Matching network topology and component values, plus harmonic/band filtering choice (discrete LC, SAW, integrated filter).
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires the network be documented but fixes no topology, impedance, or values.

open_decisions.decision: Antenna path arrangement: shared TX/RX path versus separate paths, switch selection, and bias/control sequencing from the MCU.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names only the SMA connector at the end of the chain and is silent on the path behind it.

open_decisions.decision: Battery input specifics — chemistry, cell count, voltage range, how the input physically terminates, and whether charging, protection, or fuel gauging are on this board.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for "a battery input" and states no chemistry, voltage, termination, or charging behaviour.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture: rail voltages, regulator topology (LDO versus switching) per rail, and how the supply holds up under transmit current pulses.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires power-current assumptions to be documented but states no rails, currents, or regulator approach.

open_decisions.decision: Whether USB-C supplies board power at all and, if it does, how it and the battery are arbitrated — ORing, priority, hot-swap behaviour, and inrush handling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires a battery input and a USB-C connector but never says USB-C powers the board, so both the existence of a second supply and any arbitration between the two are unstated.

open_decisions.decision: USB-C role and configuration: whether it carries data, supplies power, or both; CC termination and current advertisement; and whether USB reaches the MCU directly or through a bridge.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the connector but assigns it no function.

open_decisions.decision: SMA connector gender and mounting — jack versus plug, edge-launch versus through-hole versus vertical, and mechanical retention against mating torque.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the connector as "an SMA antenna connector" but states no gender, orientation, or mechanical constraint; the connector type itself is not open.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting holes, enclosure interface, and connector edge placement.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical envelope, size, or mounting scheme at all.

open_decisions.decision: Layer count and stackup detail beyond the metadata's likely 4 layers: dielectric material and thickness, copper weights, layer ordering, and the controlled-impedance target for the RF trace.
open_decisions.why_open: Layer count is benchmark metadata guidance stated as "likely" rather than a brief-stated constraint, and no impedance or material is specified anywhere.

open_decisions.decision: RF/digital partitioning strategy: placement zoning, ground pour and stitching scheme, return-path management, and whether a shield can is used.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mandates following vendor reference layouts but does not say how the digital side is separated from the RF side on this particular board.

open_decisions.decision: Protection strategy for the antenna port, USB-C, and the battery input — ESD, reverse polarity, overcurrent — and the capacitance budget any RF-path protection consumes.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief imposes no protection requirement; nothing in it names ESD, surge, or fault handling.

open_decisions.decision: Regulatory posture for the 902–928 MHz band: which rule set and limits the design targets, duty-cycle and spurious-emission strategy, and whether certification is in scope.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names the band only; it states no regulatory regime, power limit, or certification goal.

open_decisions.decision: What the node actually telemeters — onboard sensors, expansion I/O, or external interfaces — and the electrical form of those interfaces.
open_decisions.why_open: "Telemetry node" describes the role, but the brief lists no sensor, payload interface, or I/O count.

open_decisions.decision: Reference clock selection: crystal versus TCXO, frequency, load capacitance, and the accuracy the chosen modulation demands.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on timing, and accuracy requirements follow from the transceiver choice, which is itself open.

open_decisions.decision: Programming, debug, and test provisions — SWD/JTAG or other access, RF test point or coupling for bring-up, and any production-test access.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists no debug or test interface among the things it requires be provided.

open_decisions.decision: Indicators and user controls (LEDs, buttons, reset) and any local status/UI behaviour.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions no human interface elements.
